CHIEF COMPLAINT
Follow-up visit to reassess the management of anxiety, sleep disturbances, persistent fatigue, and headache symptoms, with particular attention to recent medication adjustments and symptom evolution.
HISTORY OF PRESENT ILLNESS
Mr. John Smith returns for a follow-up appointment, reporting a mixed response to the recent treatment modifications. He states that while there has been a slight improvement in his sleep duration, with an average of 6-7 hours per night, he still experiences frequent awakenings, especially around 3 AM, which significantly affects his overall restfulness. He acknowledges that the increased lorazepam usage has provided some relief during high-stress periods, but he remains concerned about dependency and the potential for increased daytime sedation.
Mr. Smith describes his fatigue as persistently debilitating, particularly during the workweek. He notes that his energy levels fluctuate significantly, often correlating with project deadlines and workplace demands. He reports that his headaches have decreased in frequency to 2-3 times per week, but the intensity remains moderate, averaging 4-6 out of 10. He continues to utilize ibuprofen 400 mg as needed, approximately 3 times weekly, and has not noted any gastrointestinal side effects thus far.
In terms of his holistic treatment approach, Mr. Smith remains committed to regular acupuncture and yoga, both of which he feels contribute positively to his mental health management. He has increased his cognitive-behavioral therapy sessions to bi-weekly, which he believes has been beneficial in addressing his anxiety and coping strategies.
PAST MEDICAL HISTORY
1. Generalized Anxiety Disorder - diagnosed in 2021 2. Insomnia - diagnosed in 2021 3. Tension-Type Headaches - diagnosed in 2021 4. Hypertension - diagnosed in 2020, currently well-controlled on lisinopril 10 mg daily
MEDICATIONS
1. Sertraline 200 mg daily 2. Trazodone 75 mg at bedtime 3. Melatonin 10 mg at bedtime 4. Lisinopril 10 mg daily 5. Ibuprofen 400 mg as needed for headache relief (usage stable) 6. Amitriptyline 40 mg nightly 7. Topiramate 50 mg daily (increased dosage) 8. Lorazepam 1 mg as needed (increased dosage)
ALLERGIES
No known drug allergies.
SOCIAL HISTORY
Mr. Smith continues to work as a software engineer, facing ongoing project deadlines that contribute to his stress levels. He engages in yoga and meditation regularly and maintains a healthy diet, focusing on whole foods and limiting processed items. He abstains from alcohol and has recently started participating in a local running group to enhance his physical activity levels.
REVIEW OF SYSTEMS
- Psychiatric: Sleep initiation difficulties persist; anxiety remains manageable with medication adjustments; no suicidal ideation or depressive symptoms reported. - Neurological: Headache frequency has decreased; intensity remains moderate; no visual changes or neurological deficits. - Cardiovascular: No chest pain, palpitations, or dyspnea. - General: Persistent fatigue; no fever or significant weight changes.
PHYSICAL EXAMINATION
- Vital Signs: BP 118/75 mmHg, HR 72 bpm, RR 16 breaths/min, Temp 98.6F - General: Alert, oriented, and appears slightly fatigued but in no acute distress. - Neurological: Cranial nerves II-XII intact; no motor or sensory deficits observed. - Cardiovascular: Regular rate and rhythm; no murmurs or gallops. - Psychiatric: Cooperative; maintains good eye contact; mood appears stable but fatigued.
ASSESSMENT AND PLAN
1. Generalized Anxiety Disorder: Continue sertraline at 200 mg daily. Maintain lorazepam at 1 mg as needed, with close monitoring for dependency. Encourage ongoing cognitive-behavioral therapy sessions. 2. Insomnia: Maintain trazodone at 75 mg; continue melatonin at 10 mg. Discuss the option of a sleep study if sleep issues remain unresolved in the next month. 3. Tension-Type Headaches: Continue amitriptyline at 40 mg nightly and topiramate at 50 mg daily. Reassess headache frequency and intensity at the next visit. 4. Persistent Fatigue: Encourage continued physical activity, mindfulness practices, and dietary optimization. Consider referral to a sleep specialist if fatigue does not improve with current interventions.
Follow-up appointment scheduled for 2029-01-01 to evaluate ongoing symptoms, assess treatment efficacy, and make further medication adjustments as necessary. Mr. Smith is advised to contact the office sooner if he experiences any exacerbation of symptoms or adverse effects from medications.
